definitions.explanation: Briefly boiling ingredients before the main cooking step to remove bitterness, excess starch, or impurities, or to soften tough vegetables. A fundamental technique in Japanese cooking.

examples.japanese: ほうれん{草|そう}を{下|した}ゆでする。
{大根|だいこん}は{下|した}ゆでしてから{煮込|にこ}む。
examples.english: Parboil the daikon before simmering it.

examples.japanese: {下|した}ゆでしておくと、{灰汁|あく}が{取|と}れて{仕上|しあ}がりがきれいになる。
examples.english: If you parboil it beforehand, it removes the bitterness and gives a cleaner finish.

notes:
USAGE:
A basic cooking term frequently found in recipes. Part of the {下|した}～ (pre-/preliminary) pattern common in cooking: {下|した}{味|あじ} (preliminary seasoning), {下|した}{処理|しょり} (preliminary preparation), {下|した}ごしらえ (food preparation).

Sometimes written as {下茹|したゆ}で with the kanji for {茹|ゆ}でる.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {野菜|やさい}を{下|した}ゆでする: to parboil vegetables
- {下|した}ゆでしておく: to parboil in advance
- {下|した}ゆでした{麺|めん}: parboiled noodles
